name: Nigel Austin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2024); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Nigel Austin is the founder and majority owner of the Cotton On clothing and stationery group. Its brands include Cotton On, Supre, Factorie and Typo.
His company has close to 1,300 stores in 17 countries with 2025 revenue of around $1.5 billion.
About half of these stores are in Australia, while the other half are spread across countries such as Singapore, South Africa and the U.S.
Founded in 1991, Austin started selling acid-washed denim jackets from the trunk of his car in his hometown southwest of Melbourne.
Now it sells inexpensive fashion basics, including T-shirts, leggings, sweatpants, shoes and underwear, as well as quirky stationery.
forbes_facts: Austin's late father, Grant Austin, ran a publicly traded clothing wholesale and import business called the Austin Group, where Austin would spend school holidays working.
In 1991 Austin set up his first store in a small space behind a butcher shop run by his grandfather and sourced merchandise from his father.

name: Kochouseph Chittilappilly
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: In 1977, Kochouseph Chittilappilly borrowed $1,500 from his father to set up a small unit to make voltage stabilizers.
Over four decades he built it into Kochi-based V-Guard Industries. The company's portfolio now includes kitchen appliances, air coolers and solar water heaters.
Chittilappily expanded into amusement parks in 2000 with Wonderla Holidays.
These days, Chittilappily is busy with his property venture, Veegaland Developers and his charitable foundation.
forbes_facts: His two sons run V-Guard and Wonderla.
He donated one of his kidneys to a poor truck driver.

name: Thomas Powell
forbes_bio: Thomas Powell is the former chairman and CEO of Houston-based electrical engineering and manufacturing company Powell Industries.
His father, William E. Powell, founded the company in 1947 as a metal-working shop.
Thomas Powell started working at the company in 1964 and was named chairman and CEO in 1984.
He served three terms as CEO before retiring from the top job for good in 2016.
He retired as a chairman in 2019 and as a director in 2022. He still owns 19% of the Nasdaq-listed company.

name: GT Dave
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2020-2021); Hurun Global (2020-2022)
forbes_bio: GT Dave started brewing kombucha in his parents' Bel Air kitchen at 16 years old in 1995.
He became the first to commercialize the fizzy drink, pioneering what's now one of the hottest categories in beverage.
Today, GT's Kombucha controls around 40% of the U.S. kombucha market, generating an estimated $275 million in annual sales.
Unlike his investor-backed competitors today, Dave still owns 100% of his company and has diversified into other drinks like CBD water.
forbes_facts: Dave never went to college and left high school early with a GED, after falling in with a crowd of rich kids with a taste for drugs.
Kombucha, an ancient fermented tea used by travelers along the Silk Road, earned a following during the AIDS epidemic as a supposed immune-booster.

name: Lennart Blecher
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2024); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Lennart Blecher joined publicly traded Swedish investment company EQT AB in 2007.
EQT has roughly $83 billion (73 billion Euros) in assets under management.
The firm primarily invests in private equity, but has also put funds into venture capital, real estate and infrastructure.
Blecher is a member of EQT's executive committee and chairs its the Infrastructure Partners Investment Committee.

name: Andrew Dudum
source_of_wealth: Hims & Hers Health, Inc. (HIMS) - Chief Executive Officer
sec_insider_companies: Hims & Hers Health, Inc. (HIMS) - Chief Executive Officer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Andrew Dudum is the cofounder and CEO of San Francisco-based telehealth company Hims & Hers.
A serial entrepreneur, Dudum cofounded Hims & Hers in 2017 with partners at the startup studio Atomic Ventures.
Started as a men's wellness platform offering easy-access prescriptions for things like hair loss and erectile dysfunction, Hims expanded into women's products in 2018.
The company renamed itself Hims & Hers in 2021 when it went public on the New York Stock Exchange.
Dudum owns more than 8% of the company plus options to acquire another 1%.
